summary: Radar for 2026-11-13, GLP-1 focus. There are three live hooks this week. (1) The FDA's class-wide NAION eye warning, issued Nov 9–10, now covers Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo. News coverage is peaking (AP, Guardian, ABC, The Hill, AAO), so a calm long video explaining the label change can still ride search demand. Use the numbers: about 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years, and call right away about sudden vision change. (2) T-REx, a tirzepatide plus resistance-training RCT in Nature Medicine on Nov 9, found about 25% less lean-mass loss with lifting. It's covered only by News-Medical and UWA so far. Our lifting-RCT Short got 16 views, so fold the trial into a broad 'keep muscle' piece rather than making it a single-trial video. (3) ObesityWeek runs Nov 14–17 in DC. Watch for a full REDEFINE 4 paper (CagriSema vs tirzepatide, randomized). If one appears, it's an EloraTZP-style fast turn within 48 h; the topline is from February, so only a new publication makes it fresh. The playbook's search formats are filled with broad, evergreen tirzepatide topics: a pen how-to (IFU only), a month-by-month what-to-expect timeline, and foods that make stomach side effects worse or better (this absorbs the burping/heartburn and nausea threads). There's also tirzepatide vs semaglutide, with SURMOUNT-5 as the anchor and a refresh from the Nature GLP1R-variant paper. Thanksgiving Shorts are held to Nov 18 or later. Felt-symptom Shorts: injection site, nausea (GIPR variant hook), hair, and heart rate (new wearable cohort). The stopping-and-mood case reports (NY Post) are caution-only. Rejected: compounded price reports, dose-skipping to stretch supply, the 'GLP-1 overdose' explainer, employer coverage cuts and other cost/business stories.
